name: Changing policy settings
purpose: Set a policy to Enabled, Disabled or Not configured with its options and comment, and move settings in or out as SPOL text.

layers.name: Dialog windows and their reactions
layers.summary: What a person sees and enters in the program's windows, and the routines that answer each click, selection and window event before handing the choices to the policy code.
layers.detail: What a person sees and enters in the program's windows, and the routines that answer each click, selection and window event before handing the choices to the policy code.

layers.name: Policy definitions and files
layers.summary: Reads the administrative template and comment files, joins them into policies, categories and products, and holds the data shapes those steps use.

rules.headline: Open File puts the whole chosen file…
rules.summary: ", restores the header "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and blank lines.
rules.detail: Open File puts the whole chosen file into the text box, replacing what was typed without asking and without checking it; Reset, after a Yes to "Are you sure you want to reset the text box?", restores the header "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and blank lines.

rules.headline: Verify reads the SPOL text and reports "Validation…
rules.detail: Verify reads the SPOL text and reports "Validation successful, N policy settings found." or "SPOL validation failed: " followed by the reason; nothing is applied.

rules.headline: Closing the policy setting dialog with Cancel…
rules.detail: Closing the policy setting dialog with Cancel is reported as a change when Apply was used earlier in that session, and as a cancel otherwise.

rules.headline: Apply accepts only SPOL text that reads correctly
rules.summary: Apply accepts only SPOL text that reads correctly; the parsed file is passed back to the main window.
rules.detail: Apply accepts only SPOL text that reads correctly; the parsed file is passed back to the main window. Invalid text is refused with "The SPOL text is invalid: " and the reason.

rules.headline: Supported on box shows the supported-on name…
rules.detail: The Supported on box shows the supported-on name of the policy and is empty when the policy names none.

rules.headline: Policy that applies to both computer and user…
rules.summary: A policy that applies to both computer and user can be edited for either, starting on Computer when no section was given
rules.detail: A policy that applies to both computer and user can be edited for either, starting on Computer when no section was given; a policy for one section is fixed to that section and the section choice is unavailable.

rules.headline: Opening Import SPOL discards any previously parsed SPOL
rules.detail: Opening Import SPOL discards any previously parsed SPOL so a cancelled session passes nothing back.

rules.headline: When the list editor is confirmed…
rules.summary: When the list editor is confirmed for a list where the person names each entry, and two entries have exactly the same name
rules.detail: When the list editor is confirmed for a list where the person names each entry, and two entries have exactly the same name, it is refused with "Multiple entries are named "<name>"! Remove or rename all but one." and nothing is returned. Names are compared exactly, so Run and run are accepted as two entries. A name cell never filled in stops the dialog with an unhandled error.

rules.headline: Pressing Escape closes Import SPOL as cancelled
rules.detail: Pressing Escape closes Import SPOL as cancelled unless text in the box is selected; when it is, Escape closes nothing.

rules.headline: Fragment text starts with the heading "Policy Plus…
rules.summary: The fragment text starts with the heading "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line only when "Include SPOL header" is ticked
rules.detail: The fragment text starts with the heading "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line only when "Include SPOL header" is ticked; otherwise only the fragment is shown.

rules.headline: When the list editor is confirmed…
rules.summary: When the list editor is confirmed for a list without names
rules.detail: When the list editor is confirmed for a list without names, every row except the empty new row at the bottom is returned in the order shown, with no check that a cell has content; a row whose value cell was never filled is returned as an empty entry. For named lists the same new row is ignored.

rules.headline: Number entered with a spin box is limited…
rules.summary: A number entered with a spin box is limited to the minimum and maximum the policy defines, in steps the presentation sets
rules.detail: A number entered with a spin box is limited to the minimum and maximum the policy defines, in steps the presentation sets, and starts at the presentation's default.

rules.headline: Category appears in the tree only when it…
rules.summary: A category appears in the tree only when it passes the visibility rule
rules.detail: A category appears in the tree only when it passes the visibility rule; each shown category gets an icon by its kind and carries its visible subcategories below it, and the tree is sorted.

rules.headline: Plain number box keeps any text a whole-number…
rules.summary: A plain number box keeps any text a whole-number reading accepts, including a leading sign or spaces; other text is replaced by the default.
rules.detail: A plain number box keeps any text a whole-number reading accepts, including a leading sign or spaces; other text is replaced by the default. A number above the maximum or below the minimum is replaced by that limit. Numbers above 2,147,483,647 are replaced by the default even when the policy maximum is higher. Only typing is restricted to digits; pasted text is not. A negative number kept where the minimum is below zero is converted to an unsigned number when applied.

rules.headline: After the category tree is rebuilt…
rules.summary: After the category tree is rebuilt from the loaded definitions, no category
rules.detail: After the category tree is rebuilt from the loaded definitions, no category, policy or highlighted item is selected and the information pane shows the empty state.

rules.headline: Keys other than digits and control keys…
rules.detail: Keys other than digits and control keys are ignored in a numeric text box.

rules.headline: When the list is rebuilt
rules.summary: When the list is rebuilt, the policy already selected is selected again and revealed only if it is still listed, that is
rules.detail: When the list is rebuilt, the policy already selected is selected again and revealed only if it is still listed, that is, it sits in the category shown and passes the visibility rule; otherwise nothing is selected. Then, if the policy is in the same category and the list still has that many rows, the earlier top row is put back, so the policy is not guaranteed to stay in view.

rules.headline: Plain text entry is limited to the maximum…
rules.detail: A plain text entry is limited to the maximum length the policy defines and starts with the presentation's default text.

rules.headline: Right pane lists the chosen category in this…
rules.summary: The right pane lists the chosen category in this order: an "Up: <parent name>" row marked "Parent" when the category has a parent
rules.detail: The right pane lists the chosen category in this order: an "Up: <parent name>" row marked "Parent" when the category has a parent, then visible subcategories by name, then visible policies by name. Each policy row shows its state and its comment text.

rules.headline: Check box starts with the presentation's default state
rules.detail: A check box starts with the presentation's default state.

rules.headline: Text entry with suggestions is limited…
rules.summary: A text entry with suggestions is limited to the maximum length the policy defines, starts with the presentation's default text, and lists the presentation's suggestions
rules.detail: A text entry with suggestions is limited to the maximum length the policy defines, starts with the presentation's default text, and lists the presentation's suggestions, sorted unless the presentation turns sorting off.

rules.headline: Category tree selection follows the category shown…
rules.detail: The category tree selection follows the category shown in the right pane.

rules.headline: Drop-down list shows the policy's choices…
rules.summary: A drop-down list shows the policy's choices by their translated names, sorted unless the presentation turns sorting off
rules.detail: A drop-down list shows the policy's choices by their translated names, sorted unless the presentation turns sorting off, and preselects the default choice when the presentation names one; otherwise nothing is selected.

rules.headline: When nothing is selected
rules.detail: When nothing is selected, the title and support lines are hidden and the pane reads "Select an item to see its description.".

rules.headline: For a selected policy the information pane shows…
rules.summary: For a selected policy the information pane shows its title, "(no requirements information)" when it has no support rule or "Requirements:" plus the support name
rules.detail: For a selected policy the information pane shows its title, "(no requirements information)" when it has no support rule or "Requirements:" plus the support name, and its explanation. A notice that the policy is a preference appears only for preferences.

rules.headline: For a selected or highlighted category the pane…
rules.summary: " ("The selected category" when highlighted but not opened) and its explanation. The counts include every policy and subcategory, hidden or not.
rules.detail: For a selected or highlighted category the pane shows its title, "This category contains N policies and M subcategories." ("The selected category" when highlighted but not opened) and its explanation. The counts include every policy and subcategory, hidden or not.

rules.headline: Category is orphaned when it has no parent…
rules.detail: A category is orphaned when it has no parent among the loaded definitions although its definition names one.

rules.headline: Category is empty when it holds no subcategories…
rules.detail: A category is empty when it holds no subcategories and no policies at all, counting hidden ones.

rules.headline: Category's icon is chosen in this order: orphaned
rules.detail: A category's icon is chosen in this order: orphaned, then empty, then normal.

rules.headline: Policy's icon is chosen in this order: preference
rules.detail: A policy's icon is chosen in this order: preference, then plain when it has no configurable elements, then "extra configuration" when it has some.

rules.headline: State shown when the dialog opens follows…
rules.summary: The state shown when the dialog opens follows the policy's present state in the source being edited: Enabled, Disabled, or Not Configured for anything else
rules.detail: The state shown when the dialog opens follows the policy's present state in the source being edited: Enabled, Disabled, or Not Configured for anything else, including an unclear state.

rules.headline: When the policy is Enabled
rules.summary: When the policy is Enabled, each option control is set to the value found in the source: numbers into number boxes
rules.detail: When the policy is Enabled, each option control is set to the value found in the source: numbers into number boxes, text into text and combo boxes, the matching item in drop-downs, true or false into check boxes, lines into multi-line boxes and the stored list into the list editor.

rules.headline: Category is visible when empty categories are switched…
rules.summary: A category is visible when empty categories are switched on.
rules.detail: A category is visible when empty categories are switched on. Otherwise it is visible only if it has at least one visible policy or one visible subcategory.

rules.headline: Policy is visible only if it applies…
rules.summary: A policy is visible only if it applies to a chosen area (user, computer or both).
rules.detail: A policy is visible only if it applies to a chosen area (user, computer or both). With "Only Filtered Policies" on, it must also pass the filter for a chosen area it applies to; passing for either one is enough.

rules.headline: When a view setting changes
rules.summary: When a view setting changes, the program moves up to the nearest visible category
rules.detail: When a view setting changes, the program moves up to the nearest visible category, drops the selected policy if the move happened or the policy is now hidden, then rebuilds the tree and list. A policy kept after the move appears in the information pane only: rebuilding the list reselects the category in the tree, which clears the selection, so its row is not highlighted.

rules.headline: OK and Apply are available only…
rules.detail: OK and Apply are available only when the chosen policy source can be written to.

rules.headline: Comment box is disabled and reads "Comments unavailable…
rules.summary: The comment box is disabled and reads "Comments unavailable for this policy source" when the source has no comments
rules.detail: The comment box is disabled and reads "Comments unavailable for this policy source" when the source has no comments; otherwise it shows the policy's stored comment, or is empty when there is none.

rules.headline: With both areas shown, a policy
rules.summary: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to both areas shows its common state followed by "(2)" when both match
rules.detail: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to both areas shows its common state followed by "(2)" when both match, the computer state followed by "(C)" when only the user is Not Configured, the user state followed by "(U)" when only the computer is Not Configured, and "Mixed" otherwise.

rules.headline: Applying a policy first forgets everything the source…
rules.summary: Applying a policy first forgets everything the source holds for it; Enabled then writes every option's current value, Disabled writes the disabled state
rules.detail: Applying a policy first forgets everything the source holds for it; Enabled then writes every option's current value, Disabled writes the disabled state, and Not Configured leaves the policy with no values.

rules.headline: When Enabled is chosen
rules.detail: When Enabled is chosen, applying writes every option of the policy whatever its value, including options never filled in.

rules.headline: With both areas shown, a policy
rules.summary: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to one area shows that area's state followed by "(C)" for computer or "(U)" for user.
rules.detail: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to one area shows that area's state followed by "(C)" for computer or "(U)" for user. With a single area shown, only that area's state is shown, without a suffix.

rules.headline: Policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled"
rules.summary: A policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled", "Not Configured" or "Unknown"
rules.detail: A policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled", "Not Configured" or "Unknown"; the computer source is read for the computer area and the user source for any other.

rules.headline: With both areas shown
rules.summary: With both areas shown, the comment column is empty when neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" when both have one
rules.detail: With both areas shown, the comment column is empty when neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" when both have one, and otherwise shows the single comment.

rules.headline: When a policy is applied and the source…
rules.summary: When a policy is applied and the source supports comments
rules.detail: When a policy is applied and the source supports comments, an empty comment box removes the policy's stored comment and any text replaces or adds it.

rules.headline: Policy's comment in one area is empty when
rules.summary: A policy's comment in one area is empty when that source has no comment file or holds no comment for the policy
rules.detail: A policy's comment in one area is empty when that source has no comment file or holds no comment for the policy, and otherwise the saved text.

rules.headline: Policy is a preference, not a managed policy
rules.detail: A policy is a preference, not a managed policy, when it names a registry key outside the three policy locations: software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies and system\currentcontrolset\policies.

rules.headline: Option controls can be edited only
rules.detail: Option controls can be edited only while Enabled is chosen; with Disabled or Not Configured they are greyed out.

rules.headline: Choosing Computer or User in the dialog switches…
rules.summary: Choosing Computer or User in the dialog switches the source, its writability and its comments to that section, and reloads the chosen state (Enabled
rules.detail: Choosing Computer or User in the dialog switches the source, its writability and its comments to that section, and reloads the chosen state (Enabled, Disabled or Not Configured) from it. Option values are replaced only for options the section stores when it is Enabled; other values typed earlier stay in the controls.

rules.headline: OK writes the policy to the source…
rules.detail: OK writes the policy to the source and closes the dialog as a change.

rules.headline: Apply writes the policy to the source
rules.detail: Apply writes the policy to the source, keeps the dialog open and records that a change was made.

rules.headline: When the policy setting dialog is closed…
rules.detail: When the policy setting dialog is closed by any other means, it is still reported as a change if Apply was used earlier.

rules.headline: Filter on managed policies hides preferences when managed…
rules.detail: A filter on managed policies hides preferences when managed policies are wanted, and hides managed policies when preferences are wanted.

rules.headline: Policy passes the filter only when it passes…
rules.detail: A policy passes the filter only when it passes every active part of it.

rules.headline: Filter on state keeps only policies whose state…
rules.detail: A filter on state keeps only policies whose state in the checked area is Configured (Enabled or Disabled), Not Configured, Disabled or Enabled, as chosen.

rules.headline: Filter on comments keeps only policies
rules.detail: A filter on comments keeps only policies that have a non-empty comment in the checked area, or only those that have none, as chosen.

rules.headline: Filter on products keeps only policies supported…
rules.summary: A filter on products keeps only policies supported by the chosen products
rules.detail: A filter on products keeps only policies supported by the chosen products, honouring the options to match any product and to include policies with blank support.

rules.headline: Policy applies to an area when its definition…
rules.detail: A policy applies to an area when its definition declares that area; a policy declared for both applies to each.

rules.headline: Importing semantic policy applies all its policies…
rules.summary: " when some failed, and the view refreshes either way.
rules.detail: Importing semantic policy applies all its policies to both sources and comments; the person sees "Semantic Policy successfully applied." or "N out of M could not be applied." when some failed, and the view refreshes either way.

rules.headline: Text of a policy description is tidied…
rules.summary: The text of a policy description is tidied for display
rules.detail: The text of a policy description is tidied for display: leading and trailing spaces are removed from every line and blank space at the end of the text is dropped.

rules.headline: When a semantic policy script fails to load
rules.detail: When a semantic policy script fails to load, the error gives the line it stopped at, in the form '(Error found on line N.)'.

rules.headline: Policy's lists of on-values and off-values count…
rules.summary: A policy's lists of on-values and off-values count as enabled or disabled evidence for each value in them that is present
rules.detail: A policy's lists of on-values and off-values count as enabled or disabled evidence for each value in them that is present, using the list's own key when it names one.

rules.headline: Semantic policy script is read in lines separated…
rules.summary: A semantic policy script is read in lines separated by carriage return and line feed.
rules.detail: A semantic policy script is read in lines separated by carriage return and line feed. A script using line feeds alone is read as one line, so it is refused with the signature message.

rules.headline: Policy with a registry value of its own…
rules.summary: A policy with a registry value of its own counts as enabled evidence when that value holds its 'on' value
rules.detail: A policy with a registry value of its own counts as enabled evidence when that value holds its 'on' value, which is the number 1 when the template gives none, and as disabled evidence when it holds its 'off' value or is marked for deletion when the template gives none.

rules.headline: For a policy's list elements
rules.summary: For a policy's list elements, a marked-for-deletion list counts as one deleted element, and a list
rules.detail: For a policy's list elements, a marked-for-deletion list counts as one deleted element, and a list that holds any values counts as a present element and cancels that deletion.

rules.headline: For a checkbox element
rules.summary: For a checkbox element: a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element.
rules.detail: For a checkbox element: a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element. Otherwise, each present off value (or off-list value) counts a tenth of a deleted element, and each present on value (or on-list value) counts one present element. A checkbox whose template declares no on value or on list adds no present evidence, even if it holds 1.

rules.headline: Semantic policy script is refused
rules.detail: A semantic policy script is refused unless its first line is 'Policy Plus Semantic Policy', with the message 'Incorrect signature.'.

rules.headline: Policy header line in a semantic policy script…
rules.summary: A policy header line in a semantic policy script is a user policy only when its first word is exactly 'U'.
rules.detail: A policy header line in a semantic policy script is a user policy only when its first word is exactly 'U'. Any other first word, including lowercase 'u' or 'User', is a machine policy. The rest of the line is the policy's identifier. A header with no space after the first word fails with a general index error, with the line number but no reason.

rules.headline: Comment line in a semantic policy script…
rules.summary: A comment line in a semantic policy script is recognised without regard to letter case.
rules.detail: A comment line in a semantic policy script is recognised without regard to letter case. A backslash followed by another backslash is one backslash, and a backslash followed by 'n' is a line break.

rules.headline: For any other element (number, text, choice
rules.summary: For any other element (number, text, choice, multi-line text), a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a value
rules.detail: For any other element (number, text, choice, multi-line text), a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a value that is present counts as a present element.

rules.headline: Comment in a semantic policy script is refused…
rules.summary: '. A backslash followed by any other character is refused with 'Unknown comment escape sequence' naming it.
rules.detail: A comment in a semantic policy script is refused when it ends with a lone backslash, with the message 'Escape sequence started at end of comment.'. A backslash followed by any other character is refused with 'Unknown comment escape sequence' naming it.

rules.headline: If any element is present
rules.summary: If any element is present, the elements add their count to the enabled evidence
rules.detail: If any element is present, the elements add their count to the enabled evidence; only when none is present do deleted elements add to the disabled evidence.

rules.headline: Policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled…
rules.summary: A policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled evidence, Disabled when disabled exceeds enabled, Not configured when there is no evidence either way
rules.detail: A policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled evidence, Disabled when disabled exceeds enabled, Not configured when there is no evidence either way, and Unclear when both are equal and above zero.

rules.headline: State in a semantic policy script must be…
rules.detail: The state in a semantic policy script must be 'Not configured', 'Enabled' or 'Disabled', regardless of case. Anything else is refused with 'Unknown policy state.'.

rules.headline: Value counts as present when
rules.summary: A value counts as present when: for a deletion marker, it is marked for deletion; for a number
rules.detail: A value counts as present when: for a deletion marker, it is marked for deletion; for a number, it exists as a whole number and equals the expected number; for text, it exists as text and equals the expected text. A value of the wrong kind is not present.

rules.headline: Settings are read only for a policy
rules.summary: Settings are read only for a policy that is Enabled.
rules.detail: Settings are read only for a policy that is Enabled. Lines under Not configured or Disabled are not read as settings but as the next policy's header.

rules.headline: When a value is marked for deletion…
rules.summary: When a value is marked for deletion in a policy file, any value or marker already held under that name is dropped first.
rules.detail: When a value is marked for deletion in a policy file, any value or marker already held under that name is dropped first. A deletion marker holding the number 32, as Microsoft does, is added unless the value is already marked or its key is cleared.

rules.headline: Setting value in a semantic policy script…
rules.summary: A setting value in a semantic policy script is read in this order.
rules.detail: A setting value in a semantic policy script is read in this order. Starting with # is a whole number, and a # value that is not a whole number fails with a conversion message. A plain non-negative number is an unsigned number. 'True' or 'False', in any letter case, is a yes/no value. Text in single quotes is text, and text in double quotes is a list of text. 'None' is an empty list. Anything else is refused with 'Unknown option data format.'.

rules.headline: When a value is forgotten in a policy…
rules.summary: When a value is forgotten in a policy file, both the value and its deletion marker are removed
rules.detail: When a value is forgotten in a policy file, both the value and its deletion marker are removed, so the policy reverts to not saying anything about it.

rules.headline: When a value is set in a policy…
rules.summary: When a value is set in a policy file, it replaces any value already held under that name.
rules.detail: When a value is set in a policy file, it replaces any value already held under that name. A deletion marker for the name is not removed.

rules.headline: Bracketed setting in a semantic policy script holds…
rules.summary: A bracketed setting in a semantic policy script holds one line per entry.
rules.detail: A bracketed setting in a semantic policy script holds one line per entry. Entries with one text are a list, entries with two texts are a table of name and value. With no entries the setting is stored with no value. For a list setting, the existing entries are then removed unless the definition keeps other entries, and nothing is written. For any other kind of setting the empty value makes the write fail.

rules.headline: List of values counts as present only…
rules.detail: A list of values counts as present only when every value in it is present.

rules.headline: Value in a policy file counts as present…
rules.detail: A value in a policy file counts as present only if it is stored and not marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Reading a value from a policy file gives…
rules.detail: Reading a value from a policy file gives nothing when the value is absent or marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Value in a policy file counts as marked…
rules.summary: A value in a policy file counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, when the key has a clear-all marker
rules.detail: A value in a policy file counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, when the key has a clear-all marker, or when a delete-values list for the key names it, regardless of case. Entries are examined in sorted order, and a value whose name sorts after the marker is stored as present and cancels the deletion, whenever it was written and whichever marker kind came before.

rules.headline: Listing the values of a key…
rules.detail: Listing the values of a key in a policy file leaves out the marker entries unless the caller asks for them.

rules.headline: Saved value of a number or text element…
rules.summary: The saved value of a number or text element is read as stored; the reading assumes the value exists and is of the right kind
rules.detail: The saved value of a number or text element is read as stored; the reading assumes the value exists and is of the right kind, and is not checked first. A checkbox is read by its own rule.

rules.headline: List element whose entries have names the person…
rules.detail: A list element whose entries have names the person provides is read as every stored name with its value, under the element's key.

rules.headline: List element whose entry names do not matter…
rules.summary: A list element whose entry names do not matter is read as a list of values: when the list has a prefix
rules.detail: A list element whose entry names do not matter is read as a list of values: when the list has a prefix, the stored values named prefix1, prefix2, and so on, in order, until the first number that is missing; otherwise every stored value name under the key.

rules.headline: Source is writable by default for Scratch space
rules.summary: A source is writable by default for Scratch space; for a registry source it is 'no writing' when the write test failed
rules.detail: A source is writable by default for Scratch space; for a registry source it is 'no writing' when the write test failed; for others it is 'no commit' when the file or hive could not be opened for writing.

rules.headline: Choice element is read as the position…
rules.summary: A choice element is read as the position of the first item whose own value is present and, when the item has a value list
rules.detail: A choice element is read as the position of the first item whose own value is present and, when the item has a value list, whose list is wholly present; when no item matches, the position is -1.

rules.headline: When a policy file is clearing a key
rules.detail: When a policy file is clearing a key, all values and markers under the key are dropped and a single clear-all marker is stored.

rules.headline: Saved value of a multi-line text element…
rules.detail: The saved value of a multi-line text element is read as stored, without first checking that it exists.

rules.headline: When a semantic policy script is applied…
rules.summary: When a semantic policy script is applied to many policies, a policy that fails is skipped and counted, and the rest are still applied.
rules.detail: When a semantic policy script is applied to many policies, a policy that fails is skipped and counted, and the rest are still applied. The caller gets only the number of failures, not which policy or why.

rules.headline: Checkbox is on when its on value…
rules.summary: A checkbox is on when its on value (or all values of its on list) is present, or, with neither defined
rules.detail: A checkbox is on when its on value (or all values of its on list) is present, or, with neither defined, when its value is 1; it is off in every other case, including when its off value is present.

rules.headline: When a key's clearance is forgotten…
rules.detail: When a key's clearance is forgotten in a policy file, every clear-all marker for that key is removed.

rules.headline: Semantic policy script applies each policy…
rules.detail: A semantic policy script applies each policy to the machine source or the user source by its section.

rules.headline: Name or description written as "$(string.<id>)" shows…
rules.summary: A name or description written as "$(string.<id>)" shows the language file's text for that id; an unknown id shows the code itself
rules.detail: A name or description written as "$(string.<id>)" shows the language file's text for that id; an unknown id shows the code itself; any other text is shown as written; an empty value stays empty.

rules.headline: When a semantic policy is applied
rules.summary: When a semantic policy is applied, a comment is stored for the policy first, only if one is given and a comment store exists
rules.detail: When a semantic policy is applied, a comment is stored for the policy first, only if one is given and a comment store exists, before the old settings are wiped and the new ones written. If the writing fails, the new comment stays against a half-written policy. An empty comment leaves any existing comment alone.

rules.headline: When a semantic policy is applied
rules.detail: When a semantic policy is applied, the policy's earlier settings are wiped first and then the stated state and settings are written.

rules.headline: Registry values a policy touches are its own…
rules.summary: The registry values a policy touches are its own value, those in its value lists
rules.detail: The registry values a policy touches are its own value, those in its value lists, those of its elements (the whole key for list elements) and those of checkbox and choice sub-lists, each counted once.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for asking whether a value is present: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for asking whether a value is present: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for reading a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for reading a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for checking whether a value will be deleted: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for checking whether a value will be deleted: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for listing a key's values: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for listing a key's values: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: When a value is saved into a REG…
rules.summary: When a value is saved into a REG file, it is ignored if a source branch is set and its key lies outside that branch.
rules.detail: When a value is saved into a REG file, it is ignored if a source branch is set and its key lies outside that branch. When no branch is set, every key is accepted. Any value already stored under that name is replaced.

rules.headline: Text read from a policy file stops…
rules.detail: Text read from a policy file stops at its first empty character, and a multiple-string value ends at its first empty string.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for forgetting a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for forgetting a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: Text stored in a policy file is written…
rules.detail: Text stored in a policy file is written in two-byte characters followed by a closing empty character.

rules.headline: When a value is deleted in a REG…
rules.summary: When a value is deleted in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it
rules.detail: When a value is deleted in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it, or if the key is already marked for removal. When no branch is set, every key is accepted. Otherwise the value is recorded as deleted.

rules.headline: When a key is cleared in a REG…
rules.summary: When a key is cleared in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it.
rules.detail: When a key is cleared in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it. When no branch is set, every key is accepted. Otherwise the key's earlier entries are replaced by a key-removal entry.

rules.headline: When a policy is forgotten
rules.summary: When a policy is forgotten
rules.detail: When a policy is forgotten, the whole key of each of its list elements is cleared and every registry value it touches is dropped from the source, so it reads as Not configured.

rules.headline: When a key's clearance is forgotten…
rules.summary: When a key's clearance is forgotten in a REG file, the key-removal entry is dropped if it exists.
rules.detail: When a key's clearance is forgotten in a REG file, the key-removal entry is dropped if it exists. The request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it. When no branch is set, every key is accepted.

rules.headline: 32-bit number is stored in a policy file…
rules.detail: A 32-bit number is stored in a policy file as 4 bytes, lowest byte first.

rules.headline: When a registry value is written…
rules.summary: When a registry value is written for a policy, a value defined as 'delete' is removed
rules.detail: When a registry value is written for a policy, a value defined as 'delete' is removed, a numeric value is saved as a 32-bit number and a text value as a text string. A policy with no value defined writes nothing.

rules.headline: 64-bit number is stored in a policy file…
rules.detail: A 64-bit number is stored in a policy file as 8 bytes, lowest byte first.

rules.headline: When a policy is set to Not configured…
rules.summary: When a policy is set to Not configured or Unknown, SetPolicyState writes and removes nothing.
rules.detail: When a policy is set to Not configured or Unknown, SetPolicyState writes and removes nothing. Callers forget the policy's old values first, so Not configured works by that removal alone.

rules.headline: Multiple-string value is stored as its strings…
rules.detail: A multiple-string value is stored as its strings each followed by an empty character, with one more empty character closing the list.

rules.headline: When a policy is set to Enabled…
rules.summary: When a policy is set to Enabled and the policy has a registry value name but defines no explicit on value
rules.detail: When a policy is set to Enabled and the policy has a registry value name but defines no explicit on value, the value is saved as the number 1.

rules.headline: When a policy is set to Enabled
rules.summary: When a policy is set to Enabled
rules.detail: When a policy is set to Enabled, its own on value is saved and any extra values listed for the on state are saved with it. A key left blank in a list falls back to the policy's key.

rules.headline: When a policy is set to Enabled
rules.summary: When a policy is set to Enabled, only the settings the person supplied are written.
rules.detail: When a policy is set to Enabled, only the settings the person supplied are written. A setting with no supplied value is left as it was.

rules.headline: Setting that names its own registry key…
rules.detail: A setting that names its own registry key is saved under that key. Otherwise it is saved under the policy's key.

rules.headline: When a number setting is saved
rules.detail: When a number setting is saved, it is written as text if the definition says to store it as text, otherwise as a 32-bit number.

rules.headline: When a checkbox setting is saved
rules.summary: When a checkbox setting is saved, a ticked box with no defined on value first saves the number 1
rules.detail: When a checkbox setting is saved, a ticked box with no defined on value first saves the number 1, and an unticked box with no defined off value first removes the value. The defined on or off value is then saved, with the extra values listed for that state, and overwrites the first step.

rules.headline: Stored policy file value is read back…
rules.summary: A stored policy file value is read back as text for text and expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number for numbers
rules.detail: A stored policy file value is read back as text for text and expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number for numbers, a list of strings for multiple strings, and raw bytes for every other type.

rules.headline: When a text setting is saved
rules.detail: When a text setting is saved, it is written as an expandable text string if the definition says so, otherwise as a plain text string.

rules.headline: When a list setting is saved…
rules.summary: When a list setting is saved and the definition does not say to keep other entries
rules.detail: When a list setting is saved and the definition does not say to keep other entries, every existing value under the list's key is removed first. A list with no supplied entries then stays empty.

rules.headline: When a list setting is saved, entries
rules.summary: When a list setting is saved, entries that carry their own names are saved under those names.
rules.detail: When a list setting is saved, entries that carry their own names are saved under those names. Otherwise each entry is numbered from 1, named with the definition's prefix plus its number, or named after its own text when the definition has no prefix.

rules.headline: Value written to a policy file is stored…
rules.summary: A value written to a policy file is stored as text, expandable text
rules.detail: A value written to a policy file is stored as text, expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number or a multiple string by its stated type. Every other type is stored as raw bytes with that type.

rules.headline: When a choice setting is saved
rules.summary: When a choice setting is saved, the value of the chosen item is saved together with any extra values that item lists.
rules.detail: When a choice setting is saved, the value of the chosen item is saved together with any extra values that item lists. When the chosen position does not exist, the code fails at that point: values already written for earlier settings of the same policy stay written and nothing undoes them, so the policy is left half set.

rules.headline: When a multi-line text setting is saved
rules.detail: When a multi-line text setting is saved, it is written as a multiple-string value.

rules.headline: When a policy is set to Disabled…
rules.summary: When a policy is set to Disabled and the definition gives no off value, its registry value is removed.
rules.detail: When a policy is set to Disabled and the definition gives no off value, its registry value is removed. A defined off value, with any extra off values, is saved instead.

rules.headline: When a policy is set to Disabled
rules.summary: When a policy is set to Disabled, each setting gets only its own removal.
rules.detail: When a policy is set to Disabled, each setting gets only its own removal. A list setting has all values under its key removed, even when its definition says to keep other entries. A checkbox with a defined off value or off list gets those saved, and every other setting has its single value removed. Extra values listed for a chosen item, a checkbox's on list and the policy's own on list are left in place.

rules.headline: When a value is deleted in the live…
rules.detail: When a value is deleted in the live registry and its key does not exist, nothing happens. A missing value is not an error.

rules.headline: In the live registry
rules.detail: In the live registry, 'forgetting' a value deletes it, because the registry cannot remember a pending deletion.

rules.headline: When a number is saved to the live…
rules.summary: When a number is saved to the live registry
rules.detail: When a number is saved to the live registry, an unsigned 32-bit or 64-bit number is converted to the signed number the registry stores with the same bits, and the key is created if missing.

rules.headline: When a policy lists no supported-on information
rules.summary: When a policy lists no supported-on information, it counts as supported only if the caller allows unlisted policies.
rules.detail: When a policy lists no supported-on information, it counts as supported only if the caller allows unlisted policies. The same applies to a support entry that names no known product.

rules.headline: Value in the live registry counts as present…
rules.summary: A value in the live registry counts as present when its key exists and, unless the value name is empty
rules.detail: A value in the live registry counts as present when its key exists and, unless the value name is empty, the key lists a value of that name, regardless of case. An empty name means the key itself.

rules.headline: Support entry for a product counts as met…
rules.summary: A support entry for a product counts as met in two cases.
rules.detail: A support entry for a product counts as met in two cases. The entry is not a version range and that exact product is among the chosen products. Or the product has versions beneath it, and any of those versions or their sub-products is chosen, even when the product itself is not.

rules.headline: Support entry for a product
rules.summary: A support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product
rules.detail: A support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product that is not itself chosen, counts as met when any version in its range, or a sub-product directly beneath one, is chosen. The range runs from the entry's minimum (0 if none) to its maximum (the highest version if none). A range entry never matches on its own product, and a product with no versions beneath it never matches this way.

rules.headline: Reading a value from the live registry gives…
rules.summary: Reading a value from the live registry gives nothing when the key is missing.
rules.detail: Reading a value from the live registry gives nothing when the key is missing. Signed numbers are returned as the unsigned numbers policies use, and environment variables in text are not expanded.

rules.headline: Support definition met a second time anywhere…
rules.summary: A support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation counts as not met, because the list of definitions seen is never emptied.
rules.detail: A support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation counts as not met, because the list of definitions seen is never emptied. Two entries that point at the same definition, with no cycle, make the second one not met.

rules.headline: When the caller asks for 'any' matching
rules.summary: When the caller asks for 'any' matching, a support definition whose logic is all-of needs every entry met
rules.detail: When the caller asks for 'any' matching, a support definition whose logic is all-of needs every entry met, and any other definition needs one entry met. When the caller does not ask for 'any', every definition, all-of included, is met by one entry. A definition with no entries, or none met, is met only when all are required. Plain product entries are checked before nested definitions.

rules.headline: Live registry never reports a value as marked…
rules.detail: The live registry never reports a value as marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Registry key counts as a policy key…
rules.summary: A registry key counts as a policy key when it is one of the three policy branches (software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies, system\currentcontrolset\policies) or lies below one
rules.detail: A registry key counts as a policy key when it is one of the three policy branches (software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies, system\currentcontrolset\policies) or lies below one, regardless of case.

rules.headline: Clearing a key in the live registry deletes…
rules.detail: Clearing a key in the live registry deletes every value in it but leaves the key and its subkeys. Forgetting a key's clearance does nothing.

risks.headline: Applying a policy file's held changes to the live registry writes, deletes or clears whatever keys the file names.
risks.summary: Only forgetting old values is limited to policy branches, so a crafted policy file, a different route from a REG import
risks.detail: Applying a policy file's held changes to the live registry writes, deletes or clears whatever keys the file names. Only forgetting old values is limited to policy branches, so a crafted policy file, a different route from a REG import, can change other registry keys.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does

risks.headline: Applying a policy, from the settings window or a script, clears its stored values or comment before the new ones are read or written.
risks.summary: A failure, such as a drop-down with no choice, leaves the policy empty or half set and reports little.
risks.detail: Applying a policy, from the settings window or a script, clears its stored values or comment before the new ones are read or written. A failure, such as a drop-down with no choice, leaves the policy empty or half set and reports little.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden.
risks.summary: An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost
risks.detail: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden. An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost, and turning on the comment filter then fails with an unhandled error.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Enabling a policy with a list option the person never opened writes that option with no list.
risks.summary: The list stays empty until the list editor is used or the source holds one, and nothing checks it.
risks.detail: Enabling a policy with a list option the person never opened writes that option with no list. The list stays empty until the list editor is used or the source holds one, and nothing checks it.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values.
risks.summary: A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.
risks.detail: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values. A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Importing a REG file applies it to whichever source is open, live registry or policy file, with no check of the keys it names.
risks.summary: The branch limit exists only when a REG file is the target, so an import can write, delete or clear keys outside the policy branches.
risks.detail: Importing a REG file applies it to whichever source is open, live registry or policy file, with no check of the keys it names. The branch limit exists only when a REG file is the target, so an import can write, delete or clear keys outside the policy branches.
risks.category: Someone can read or change what they should not

risks.headline: Results of requesting Windows privileges and loading a user registry file are discarded.
risks.summary: The person learns a source cannot be saved, or silently gets an empty read-only source, never why.
risks.detail: Results of requesting Windows privileges and loading a user registry file are discarded. The person learns a source cannot be saved, or silently gets an empty read-only source, never why. A refused privilege passes silently and fails later with an unrelated error.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Values supplied for a policy's settings, by a person or a script, are written without checks.
risks.summary: Numbers are forced to unsigned 32-bit and text is stored as given, ignoring any minimum, maximum or length in the definition.
risks.detail: Values supplied for a policy's settings, by a person or a script, are written without checks. Numbers are forced to unsigned 32-bit and text is stored as given, ignoring any minimum, maximum or length in the definition. A failure leaves earlier settings written, with no undo.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does

risks.headline: When rights or a per-user registry file cannot be obtained, the results are discarded.
risks.summary: The person is told a source cannot be modified or saved, never why, and can keep editing an empty in-memory source that is never written.
risks.detail: When rights or a per-user registry file cannot be obtained, the results are discarded. The person is told a source cannot be modified or saved, never why, and can keep editing an empty in-memory source that is never written.
